AutoDiscovery RL — training dynamics & task quality
autodiscovery RL · training dynamics & task quality

Training-dynamics & task-quality analysis

Part 1: six metrics across three same-setup cohorts. Part 2: per-task training quality — which datasets are worth training on.

1 · Training dynamics (same-setup cohorts)

Rows = cohorts. Columns = rollout reward, response length, entropy loss, surprise ratio (frac. reward ≥ 0.2), positive-surprisal ratio (Δbelief > 0), and valid surprises in prompt (avg # non-n/a surprise scores shown in the ancestor history). Bold = EMA-smoothed; faint = raw. Reward = |normalized surprisal| for all runs.

Reward scale: normalized |surprisal| for every run; the (b) ≈0.24 vs (c) ≈0.8 gap is different run batches/config, not a reward-signal change — comparisons stay within a panel.
Surprise vs. positive-surprisal: surprise ratio ~0.35–0.65, but positive-surprisal is tiny (~0.02–0.13) — most reward-earning surprises are negative belief updates. Exception: lr 5e-6·KL 0.001 (a) climbs to ~0.3.
fmt1 vs fmt2/fmt3 (valid surprises in prompt): fmt1_hyps_open shows 0 — its prompt lists prior hypotheses with no surprise scores — while fmt2/fmt3 both show ~0.85 valid surprise scores per prompt (they render (hypothesis, surprise) pairs). So fmt1 conditions on no surprise signal; fmt2 and fmt3 are equivalent on this axis.

(a) LR + KL-coeff

KL 0.001+lr 4e-6 climbs best; KL 0.03 flat/declines. lr 5e-6·KL 0.03 collapses (entropy → ~1.8, length blow-up). All fmt1 → 0 valid surprises in prompt.

(b) Format Effect

fmt1/2/3 ~flat near 0.24 reward. Key split: fmt1 = 0 surprises in prompt, fmt2 ≈ fmt3 ≈ 0.85. w_verdict slightly higher surprise ratio.

(c) Verdict Effect

Mixed reward — no consistent verdict advantage; pairs vs w_verdict track together on ratios and prompt surprises (~0.85).

(d) Execution Model (luna vs mini) — omitted: no valid pair with both runs after the review-prompt fix (fa0f6de, 2026-08-04 ~18:34 UTC). At fmt1·5e-6·KL0.03 only luna (oq07ja4j) is post-fix; every mini run predates it.

2 · Per-task training quality

Reward, surprise ratio, and reward-server invalid rate pooled per dataset over all 40 runs. Some tasks are low quality: the reviewer rarely finds anything surprising, and/or the reward server fails to score most rollouts — both waste training signal.

Removal candidates: amtl is worst on both axes — 23.6% surprise, 66.6% invalid. The bottom cluster — amtl, conversation, requirements_engineering, worldbank_education_gdp, archaeology (+ soccer at 54% invalid) — combine low surprise with ~50–67% wasted rollouts. Dropping these removes a large chunk of no-signal / failed-reward samples.
